experiment_description: Computational determination of the zero-field Rydberg-series energies of neutral two-dimensional excitons in monolayer WSe2 for zero center-of-mass momentum. The exciton was modeled within the effective-mass approximation using electron mass me = 0.29 m0, hole mass mh = 0.64 m0, reduced mass mr defined by 1/mr = 1/me + 1/mh, Keldysh screening length r0 = 5 nm, and surrounding relative dielectric constant epsilon_v = 3.97, representative of hBN encapsulation. At B = 0 T the Hamiltonian was H0 = pe^2/(2me) + ph^2/(2mh) + V(r), where r is the electron-hole separation and V(r) is the Keldysh interaction V(r) = -e^2/[8 epsilon0 r0] * [H0_special(epsilon_v r/r0) - Y0_special(epsilon_v r/r0)], with H0_special the Struve function and Y0_special the Bessel function of the second kind. The radial Schrödinger equation was solved in real space for s exciton states with magnetic quantum number l = 0 and principal quantum numbers n = 1, 2, 3, and 4. The radial coordinate was represented on an equidistant grid with spacing delta_r = 0.05 nm from r = 0 to cutoff rcut = 60 nm, using boundary conditions R(rcut) = 0 and dR/dr at r = 0 equal to 0. The generalized finite-difference eigenvalue problem was solved numerically; reported eigenenergies are relative to the free electron-hole continuum, so bound states have negative energies.

experiment_description: Computational determination of intrinsic exciton diamagnetic coefficients and root-mean-square electron-hole radii in monolayer WSe2 from zero-field wavefunctions. The same effective-mass Keldysh exciton model was used: electron mass me = 0.29 m0, hole mass mh = 0.64 m0, reduced mass mr satisfying 1/mr = 1/me + 1/mh, screening length r0 = 5 nm, and surrounding relative dielectric constant epsilon_v = 3.97. Zero-center-of-mass exciton radial wavefunctions R_nl(r) were obtained by solving the B = 0 T radial Schrödinger equation in real space on an equidistant radial grid with delta_r = 0.05 nm and cutoff rcut = 60 nm, with R(rcut) = 0 and dR/dr at r = 0 equal to 0. Exciton states were labeled by principal quantum number n and angular state s, p, d, or f corresponding to |l| = 0, 1, 2, or 3. For each state, the mean-square electron-hole separation was computed from <r_nl^2> = integral_0^infinity dr r^3 R_nl(r)^2. The root-mean-square radius was r_nl = sqrt(<r_nl^2>). The low-field diamagnetic coefficient sigma_nl was obtained from the quadratic diamagnetic shift relation Delta_epsilon_dia_nl(B) = sigma_nl B^2 = [e^2 <r_nl^2>/(8 mr)] B^2. Only the zero-field-wavefunction-derived values, not the high-field quadratic-fit values or cited external experimental data, are reported.

experiment_description: Computational comparison of the magnetic-field splitting between positive- and negative-angular-momentum exciton states in monolayer WSe2. The exciton was modeled with electron mass me = 0.29 m0, hole mass mh = 0.64 m0, Keldysh screening length r0 = 5 nm, and relative dielectric constant epsilon_v = 3.97. A perpendicular magnetic field B was swept over the range 0 to 65 T. In real space, the zero-center-of-mass relative-motion radial equation included the kinetic term, Keldysh interaction, angular-momentum magnetic-moment term proportional to l B, and diamagnetic confinement term proportional to B^2 r^2, using radial grid spacing delta_r = 0.05 nm and cutoff rcut = 60 nm. In the Landau-quantization-space calculation, free electron-hole Landau-level product states were used as a basis with matrix dimension cutoff Ncut = 300, and the Coulomb matrix elements were evaluated with the same Keldysh interaction. The exciton energy epsilon_nl(B) denotes the eigenenergy of the state with principal quantum number n and magnetic quantum number l at field B. The measured splitting Delta_epsilon_nl(B) is defined as epsilon_n,+l(B) minus epsilon_n,-l(B), for positive integer l. The angular frequencies are omega_e = e B / me and omega_h = e B / mh, where e is the elementary charge; hbar is the reduced Planck constant. The compared states used l = 1, 2, and 3 across multiple n values.

positive_negative_l_exciton_energy_split.description: Magnetic-field-dependent energy difference between exciton states with opposite magnetic quantum numbers, found to be independent of principal quantum number n and linear in both magnetic field B and l.
